motivation: Return-fragility and recovery-debt analyses independently show that re-recorded Thalassia is both more likely to be lost again and quantitatively depressed. Test whether return-year quantitative state predicts the subsequent re-loss within recovered points after previously identified legacy/community covariates are represented.

primary_population.years: t, t+1, t+2, t+3 observed consecutively at same point
primary_population.pattern: Thalassia present t, absent t+1, present t+2
primary_population.required_history: pre-loss consecutive Thalassia run length ending at t
primary_population.required_loss_state: whether another seagrass remained at t+1

primary_hypothesis.statement: Among recovered exact points, lower return-year Thalassia Braun-Blanquet state predicts greater next-year recorded re-loss after stable node, return year, pre-loss focal history, loss-year vegetation continuity, and source point abundance are represented.
primary_hypothesis.direction: negative coefficient = higher return abundance associated with lower re-loss risk
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: upper bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for return_bb coefficient < 0

secondary: raw re-loss fraction by return-year Braun-Blanquet quartile if each quartile has >=10 sequences; descriptive only
model coefficient for pre-loss run length
model coefficient for loss-year vegetation continuity
return-year Braun-Blanquet mean among stable versus re-lost returns

interpretation.supported: Quantitative quality of re-recorded Thalassia predicts subsequent stability: higher return-year abundance is associated with lower next-year re-loss, linking recovery debt to binary return fragility.
interpretation.unsupported: Return-year Braun-Blanquet state does not add robust information about subsequent re-loss after legacy, loss-year vegetation, site identity, year, and source abundance are represented; recovery debt and return fragility remain parallel rather than demonstrably linked.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc fragility mechanism-discrimination on an already-opened exact-point recovery endpoint.
A supported return-quality coefficient would not prove that low abundance causes re-loss; both can reflect residual stress, microsite quality, detectability, or demographic state.
Braun-Blanquet is ordinal abundance, not percent cover or biomass.
Recorded re-loss is an observation-state transition, not mortality or demographic relapse.

Do not change the recovered pattern, period, history definition, loss-year state, quantitative inclusion rule, controls, model, minima, or directional support threshold after opening re-loss by return quality.
